title: Build an Event Announcement Generator
summary: Build one stable part of an event announcement at a time, carrying every completed value and decision into the next step.

sketchBlocks.title: Project brief: Event Announcement Generator
Move from event facts to one final message

quizDraft.title: Step 1: Store the event identity
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The campus announcement cannot describe an event until the program knows which event it is talking about and where it takes place. Task: Create only `eventName` and `location` as constants. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the event identity is stored; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: This step stores only the two text facts that identify the event.

help.hint_1: Use const for facts that do not change.
help.hint_2: Create one constant for the name and one for the location.

quizDraft.title: Step 2: Store registration numbers
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The announcement will eventually tell students whether space is available, but the program first needs the total capacity and current registration count. Task: Keep the complete Step 1 code and add only `capacity` and `registered` as number constants. Expected result: Check Answer confirms both registration numbers are available; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: Add the source numbers without calculating anything yet.

quizDraft.title: Step 3: Calculate remaining seats
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: Raw capacity and registration counts do not directly tell a student how many seats are still open. Task: Keep all previous values and add only `seatsRemaining = capacity - registered`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the project can derive the remaining-seat count; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: Use the two registration numbers already stored.

help.concept: derive one value from existing data
help.hint_1: Open seats equal capacity minus registered.

quizDraft.title: Step 4: Store the deadline state
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: Available seats alone are not enough to decide whether registration is open because the signup deadline may already have passed. Task: Keep the complete previous solution and add only the boolean `deadlinePassed`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the project can represent the deadline state; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: Add one boolean fact and no decision logic yet.

help.hint_2: For the supplied event, keep the deadline active.

quizDraft.title: Step 5: Calculate whether registration is open
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The program now knows seat availability and deadline state, but it still needs one clear rule for whether a student may register. Task: Add only `isOpen` so registration is open when seats remain and the deadline has not passed. Expected result: Check Answer confirms the complete availability rule; the Console stays unchanged.

quizDraft.title: Step 6: Choose the status text
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The boolean `isOpen` is useful to code, but students need a readable registration message. Task: Keep the complete availability rule and add `statusText` with one `if/else` that assigns `Registration open` or `Registration closed`. Expected result: Check Answer confirms both readable decision branches; the Console stays unchanged.
quizDraft.hint: Translate the completed boolean into readable text.

help.concept: turn a boolean decision into user-facing text
help.hint_2: Use isOpen directly in the if.

quizDraft.title: Step 7: Build the final announcement
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: The project now has all of the facts and decisions, but they are still separate values instead of one announcement a student can read. Task: Add only the `announcement` template literal using the event name, location, status text, and remaining seats. Expected result: Check Answer confirms one complete announcement string is assembled; nothing is logged yet.
